title: From West Africa to Palestine
publisher: T. J. Sawyer; John Heywood; Simpkin, Marshall, & Co.

history.note: Printed page 16: the paragraph continued from the page before is joined to it again (the corrections pass had split it).

summary: Edward W. Blyden, a scholar and Presbyterian minister born in the Danish West Indies who had settled in Liberia, left Monrovia in June 1866 to see Egypt and the Holy Land. The book is his journal of the journey, kept for friends at home: by steamer along the coast to Sherbro’, Sierra Leone, and the Gambia, by Teneriffe and Madeira to Liverpool, some weeks in London (the House of Commons, a reading by Charles Dickens, a meeting of the Royal Geographical Society), then by the P. and O. line to Gibraltar, Malta, and Alexandria. In Egypt he visits Cairo and the Pyramids, which he argues were built by ancient Negroes; then Beirut and Mount Lebanon, Jaffa, Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and Bethany. The last chapter describes the religious sects of the Holy Land.
